You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer scripts):
- file: config.env.example:8
- category: stale-doc
- title: Header claims 'an exported value in your shell takes precedence' -- false for the setup.sh path
- detail: Lines 7-9 say 'Both setup.sh and the test harness scripts load ./config.env at startup, so an exported value in your shell takes precedence; this file fills in the gaps'. That is true for tests/lib/paths.sh (sources config.env only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is unset, lines 17-19) and for scripts/build_runtime.sh (captures exported values first, lines 21-34), but false for setup.sh: it sources config.env unconditionally (setup.sh line 76), and config.env's plain assignments (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=..., QEMU_BIN_DIR=..., VSIM_BIN_DIR=...) overwrite any exported value. A user exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR to point at a different QEMU and then running `source ./setup.sh` silently gets the config.env value instead, contrary to this comment. Structural fix: correct the comment to state that setup.sh always takes the config.env values (or scope the precedence claim to the harness scripts). Making setup.sh honor the environment would be a behavioral change and is out of scope here; this pairs with the env-resolution consolidation finding in build_runtime.sh.
- claimed safety: Comment-only edit in a template file that is copied verbatim to the gitignored config.env; no script reads the comments.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
3	# external build dirs to PATH.
4	# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
5	#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
6	#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)
7	
8	if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
9	  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
10	elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
11	  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
12	else
13	  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
14	fi
15	
16	# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
17	# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
18	# under nounset).
19	_hybrid_setup_main() {
20	  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
21	    emulate -L sh
22	    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
23	  else
24	    local -
25	    set -euo pipefail
26	  fi
27	
28	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
29	  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
30	  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
31	  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
32	  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
33	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
34	  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
35	  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
36	  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
37	  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
38	  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
39	  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
40	
41	  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
42	  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
43	  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	
45	  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
46	  clean_plugin() {
47	    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
48	    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
49	      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
50	    else
51	      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
52	    fi
53	    ok "plugin cleaned"
54	  }
55	
56	  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
57	    case "${2:-all}" in
58	      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
59	      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
60	      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
61	      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	  fi
65	
66	  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
67	  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
68	    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
69	      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
70	      return 1
71	    fi
72	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
73	    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
74	  fi
75	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
76	  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
77	  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
78	    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
79	    return 1
80	  fi
81	  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
82	    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
83	    return 1
84	  fi
85	  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
86	  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
87	
88	  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
89	  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
90	    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
91	    return 1
92	  fi
93	  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
94	    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
95	      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
96	      return 1
97	    fi
98	  done
99	  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"
100	
101	  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
102	  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
103	    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
104	    return 1
105	  fi
106	  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
107	    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
108	    return 1
109	  fi
110	  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"
111	
112	  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
113	  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
114	    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
115	    return 1
116	  fi
117	  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
118	  # QEMU source tree required.
119	  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
120	  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"
121	
122	  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
123	  case ":$PATH:" in
124	    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
125	    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
126	  esac
127	  case ":$PATH:" in
128	    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
129	    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
130	  esac
131	  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"
132	
133	  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
134	  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
135	  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
136	  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
137	  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
138	  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
139	  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
140	  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
141	  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
142	  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
143	  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"
144	
145	  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
146	    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
147	    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
148	  fi
149	}
150	
151	_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
152	unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
153	unset _SETUP_SRC

1	# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
2	# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
3	#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
4	#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
5	#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
6	#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
7	#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
8	#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
9	#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
10	#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
11	#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
12	#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
13	
14	TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	
17	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
18	  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
19	fi
20	
21	hybrid_resolve_paths() {
22	  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
23	  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
24	  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
25	  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
26	  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
27	  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
28	  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
29	  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
30	    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
31	      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
32	      exit 77
33	    fi
34	  done
35	}
36	
37	# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
38	# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
39	# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
40	hybrid_describe_int() {
41	  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
42	    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
43	}
44	
45	# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
46	# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
47	put_word_le() {
48	  local v=$3 bytes="" i
49	  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
50	    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
51	  done
52	  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
53	  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
54	}

2	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
3	#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
4	#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
5	#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
6	# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 4).
7	#
8	# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
9	# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
10	# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
14	SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
15	CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
16	CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
17	
18	[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
19	
20	# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
21	ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
22	ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
23	if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
24	  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
25	    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
26	      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
27	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"

29	  fi
30	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
31	  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
32	fi
33	[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
34	[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
35	
36	# rv64 (required).
37	if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
38	  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
39	  exit 1
40	fi
41	make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
42	echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
43	
44	# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
45	if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
46	  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
47	  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
48	else
49	  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
50	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# setup.sh env contract: after `source ./setup.sh`, QEMU_BIN_DIR /
3	# VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_PLUGIN must be EXPORTED -- i.e. visible to
4	# CHILD processes, because that is how they are consumed (`bash
5	# scripts/run_e2e.sh`, the driver, the test harnesses all read the
6	# environment).
7	#
8	# Regression: QEMU_BIN_DIR/VSIM_BIN_DIR were declared `local` inside
9	# _hybrid_setup_main and exported later in the same function -- exporting a
10	# local dies at function return, so the sourcing shell kept only VSIM_QEMU/
11	# VSIM_PLUGIN (never in the local list). Worse, HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN survived,
12	# which makes tests/lib/paths.sh skip its config.env fallback: a
13	# setup.sh-sourced shell was strictly WORSE off than a fresh one, and
14	# run_e2e.sh silently fell back to the legacy in-tree vsim path.
15	
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
19	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
20	
21	# Source in a clean bash, then read the vars from a CHILD of that shell.
22	out=$(env -u QEMU_BIN_DIR -u VSIM_BIN_DIR -u VSIM_QEMU -u VSIM_PLUGIN \
23	      bash -c "cd '$ROOT' && source ./setup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1;
24	               bash -c 'printf \"%s|%s|%s|%s\" \
25	                 \"\${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}\" \"\${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}\" \
26	                 \"\${VSIM_QEMU:-}\" \"\${VSIM_PLUGIN:-}\"'")
27	IFS='|' read -r qemu_dir vsim_dir vsim_qemu vsim_plugin <<<"$out"
28	
29	fail() { echo "FAIL[setup_exports]: $*"; exit 1; }
30	
31	[ -n "$qemu_dir" ]    || fail "QEMU_BIN_DIR not exported to children"
32	[ -n "$vsim_dir" ]    || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR not exported to children"
33	[ -n "$vsim_qemu" ]   || fail "VSIM_QEMU not exported to children"
34	[ -n "$vsim_plugin" ] || fail "VSIM_PLUGIN not exported to children"
35	[ -d "$vsim_dir" ]    || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$vsim_dir is not a directory"
36	ls "$vsim_dir"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1 \
37	  || fail "no sim_* under exported VSIM_BIN_DIR=$vsim_dir"
38	
39	echo "PASS[setup_exports]"
